newsitem.title: UK: EMAP seeks to remove rebel non-execs.
newsitem.headline: EMAP seeks to remove rebel non-execs.

text.p: Media group EMAP Plc will try to end a damaging boardroom row when it holds an extraordinary meeting on Monday, at which it will seek the removal of two rebel non-executive directors.
Ken Simmonds and Joe Cooke, the pair at the centre of the dispute, have led the opposition to changes made to the company's articles at its annual meeting in July.
The controversial changes remove a requirement to maintain at least five non-executive directors and allow a director to be ousted if 75 percent of the board vote for his removal.
Separate votes on the removal of Simmonds and Cooke are the only items on the agenda at the EGM, to be held in a central London hotel on Monday morning.
The row has hit EMAP shares, which have fallen to 732-1/2p from 783p in early October, despite a strong first-half profit performance from the radio, magazines and exhibitions group.

Analysts fear that there are simmering tensions between chief executive Robin Miller and managing director David Arculus over strategy. However, the board has united behind chairman Sir John Hoskyns in his battle to oust the rebel duo.
Finance director David Grigson recently told Reuters he believed the EGM would bring the bust-up to a conclusion.
"The EGM will be a purging process. It will clear the air and leave us with a smaller and happier board," he said.
Simmonds and Cooke argue that their removal would be a setback for ordinary shareholders.

"A vote in favour of our removal would undermine the fundamental principle that public companies should have independent non-executive directors who are prepared to speak out for what they believe to be in shareholders' interests," they said in a letter to all EMAP shareholders.
